# External Cicada research repositories and historical archive

These are useful independent research and historical references. They are not authoritative proof of an LP2 solution; preserve the distinction between archived facts, community transcription, simulations, and hypotheses.

## micheloosterhof/cicada-2014 (contemporaneous 2014 participant archive)

Repository: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014

The pinned 13 February 2014 commit (https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014/commit/2547f5f08f06f8f514329c5d533b0a99968e365e), authored by micheloosterhof, contains the first 2014 onion service's root page and linked image under stage2/:

- Root HTML: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014/blob/2547f5f08f06f8f514329c5d533b0a99968e365e/stage2/index.html — 104 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 807541d764ed33c976717b7ee2d08ac0720ce56b; title “For Every Thing That Lives Is Holy,” with an image link to 1033.jpg.
- Linked image: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014/blob/2547f5f08f06f8f514329c5d533b0a99968e365e/stage2/1033.jpg — 342,361 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 90d04bc54e9a35e3171a92386b5932a2dfb8e98f. The SHA-256 recorded for the same blob in the Dukotah mirror manifest is 15b2b99fe15ff34ef3eab574bb84bfaad0a119674be2ca5baf65951e6a9bd865.
- Stage 2 README: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014/blob/2547f5f08f06f8f514329c5d533b0a99968e365e/stage2/README.md — directs solvers to fetch http://auqgnxjtvdbll3pv.onion/ and /1033.jpg, run OutGuess, verify the PGP signature, then decrypt the RSA message.
- Preserved OutGuess output: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/cicada-2014/blob/2547f5f08f06f8f514329c5d533b0a99968e365e/stage2/1033.jpg.outguess — 1,498-byte signed RSA-OAEP challenge, Git blob SHA-1 cd529671eac6458a790f047d23895af264b11751; byte-identical to the signed 1033.jpg.asc in the pinned neuroretransmit archive: https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/002-first-onion/1033.jpg.asc.

The root HTML and image blob IDs also match the later iBotPeaches onion snapshot (https://github.com/iBotPeaches/cicada_3301/tree/09a6fa4848e5943dbb48c738584f2ec8442ec2a4/onions/auqgnxjtvdbll3pv.onion/post) and krisyotam mirror (https://github.com/krisyotam/cicada3301/tree/76d3ee8c762f60025822c8c05edbf31351636469/puzzles/2014/assets/stage02/auqgnxjtvdbll3pv.onion). These are byte-identity corroboration, not independent custody. Treat the 2014 GitHub snapshot as a contemporaneous participant archive: it proves the files were present by that commit, but preserves neither HTTP response headers nor a Cicada-signed HTML response.

The source-only RSA handoff audit is negative. The 2014-02-13 stage2 tree contains exactly four files: index.html, 1033.jpg, 1033.jpg.outguess and README.md; it has no numbers.private, numbers.public, armored.pem or key-reconstruction script. The later [neuroretransmit 2024 snapshot](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/tree/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/002-first-onion) contains a community-generated numbers.private object and [recreate-pk-decrypt.pl](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/002-first-onion/recreate-pk-decrypt.pl), which accepts decimal p and q and constructs a Crypt::RSA private key. Its README says the factors were obtained by GNFS; this is a solver-derived key, not an authenticated Cicada secret. The companion [recreate-armor.py](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/002-first-onion/recreate-armor.py) hard-codes a different 432-bit modulus from the signed Stage2 modulus, so its PEM output is not accepted as matching-key evidence.

## pnotisdev/cicada3301

Repository: https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301

A large, staged research notebook with a substantial catalogue of controlled tests and an explicit unresolved frontier. Its reported status is no verified LP2 plaintext. Use it to avoid repeating screened key-source and mechanism families.

Relevant material:

- [Source registry](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/main/docs/SOURCES.md) and [phase 31 book-code analysis](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/main/work/log/phase31_book_codes.md): the 2014 Gödel, Escher, Bach book code uses dialogue:speech:word:letter coordinates. The book is named by a preceding clue chain; this is not a reason to use GEB as an LP2 key without a comparable LP2 source cue.
- [Phase 57 mechanism model](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/main/work/log/phase57_mechanism.md): a candidate forward model combines a lag-six (T(x)=24-2x) collision repair (reported repair probability about 0.81) with a checked, uniformly valued word-null insertion (reported probability about 0.42). It fits a set of aggregate ciphertext statistics in the authors' simulations, but supplies neither an authentic key nor plaintext. Treat it as a competing explanatory model, not an established mechanism.
- [Phase 58 repeated-pair report](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/main/work/log/phase58_djubei_reuse.md): reports the two `DJU BEI` occurrences at offsets 6555 and 12950.
- [Phase 61 unrepair test](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/main/work/log/phase61_unrepair.md): naive replacement of detected lag-six sites loses information; a repair-aware likelihood improves planted-key simulations but does not recover a real key.
- The lag-six observation overlaps this repository's existing held-out analysis in `im-results/lag5-lag6-heldout-conditional-prediction.md`; use the external result as independent corroboration, not as a new discovery.
- [Phase 52 Wayback CDX index](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/15200c67abee106913ba01ff504c5b6e88d16cc7/work/phase52/cdx_results.json), [query script](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/15200c67abee106913ba01ff504c5b6e88d16cc7/work/phase52/cdx_query.py), [raw replay script](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/15200c67abee106913ba01ff504c5b6e88d16cc7/work/phase52/wb_fetch.py), and [Phase 52 report](https://github.com/pnotisdev/cicada3301/blob/15200c67abee106913ba01ff504c5b6e88d16cc7/work/log/phase52_an_end_archives.md): this is Wayback CDX metadata (862 queries, 15,289 rows, 71 URL hosts, 34 candidate v2 onion labels; 2008-02-13–2026-10-11), not a separate WARC index. CDX fields are timestamp/original/mimetype/statuscode/digest/length; there are no WARC filename/offset fields. Five requests for the exact p56 hash path on the exploratory, unsigned cicada3301.org domain are all 404/522 (2016-04-12–2017-05-09). The signed 2016 message does not name this domain. Phase52's 124,017-digest/3,739-file scan found no p56 match, but its body fetcher excludes cicada3301.org root pages, leaving its root HTML payloads outside the body scan. Known 2014 Cicada onion names appear through gateway domains only; no authenticated 2016 service host or target page was recovered.
- **cicada3301.org root-capture follow-up (21 November 2026):** the Phase 52 CDX query contains 257 exact root-URL records (2015-08-14–2026-06-29; 159 status 200, 59 status 302, 7 status 523, 32 revisits). A separate pinned [Dukotah CDX index](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/7a264cb643c7e6a3076a318e82734472da37ee5d/corpus/D-archives/cdx/cicada3301.org.json) has 208 exact root records (148 status 200, 50 status 302, 2 status 523, 8 revisits); its 2015–2017 subset is 14 captures, 13 status 200 and one revisit. The exact p56 digest path itself remains 404/522 in both indexes (five Phase 52 captures; four Dukotah captures). A separate [ArchiveTeam WARC metadata record](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/7a264cb643c7e6a3076a318e82734472da37ee5d/corpus/D-archives/iarchive/meta_warc-cicada3301_org.json) describes a 2016-11-26 crawl seeded at the HTTPS root: the 23-byte start-URL SHA-1 matches https://cicada3301.org/; the WARC is 16,512,716 bytes and the item reports imagecount 359, but the item and every file are private/access-restricted. A pinned [2024 snapshot](https://github.com/RYSF13/cicada3301/tree/52fce6439eed12de73063daac4ee34ff4d4dc26c) is branded “Cicadian” and marks its Liber Primus/Gematria pages “coming soon”; this later community snapshot is not evidence of 2016 first-party authorship. The root HTML bodies remain unavailable, so this domain is not an authenticated Cicada destination.

## neuroretransmit/cicada (2013 onion archive)

Repository: https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada

A stage-by-stage community archive of the 2013 round. Three first/second-onion cleartext-signed messages are mirrored under `resources/historical/` and verify against the repository's Cicada public key (fingerprint `6D85 4CD7 9333 22A6 01C3 286D 181F 01E5 7A35 090F`):

- [First-onion hello](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/main/2013/004-first-onion/hello.txt.asc): signature dated 6 January 2013 07:51:35 UTC; names `xsxnaksict6egxkq.onion`.
- [Second-onion ICMP reply](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/main/2013/005-second-onion/icmp-echo.asc): signature dated 10 January 2013 17:07:15 UTC; names `pklmx2eeh6fjt7zf.onion`.
- [Second-onion instruction](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/main/2013/005-second-onion/everything-you-need.txt.asc): signature dated 14 January 2013 05:31:07 UTC; says solvers already have what they need and to "knock on the sky and listen to the sound."
- The companion first-onion [forest clue](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/main/2013/004-first-onion/clue.txt.asc) is already mirrored as `resources/historical/cicada2013-forest-clue.asc`.

The archive's first-onion `server.py` and `gematria.py` explicitly describe themselves as recreations from publicly known behavior, not recovered original server source. Treat its COUNT/NUMBER implementation details as reconstructed, not as an authenticated Cicada implementation. The whitespace visible in the first-onion cleartext-signed hello file is not protected by OpenPGP cleartext-signature trailing-whitespace canonicalization; do not promote whitespace counts as signed evidence.

The [third-onion archive](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/tree/main/2013/006-third-onion) preserves the coordinate, poster, phone, XOR-offset and Shamir-share stages. The [fourth-onion archive](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/tree/main/2013/007-fourth-onion) is explicitly leak-based and largely undocumented; its 19-question images are not, by themselves, evidence of an LP2 key or selector.



**Participant DH-session log census (2024 archive custody).** The pinned neuroretransmit/cicada archive commit ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3 contains exactly ten irc-logs/clientlog-* files. The complete finite census, byte counts, Git blob SHA-1s and raw SHA-256s are preserved in 2013-tcp-live-test-vectors.json. The 26 January DH 118818811 transcript is 1,759 bytes (Git blob SHA-1 8c0a93d7d620c35805d9be71206d593df8e15dca; SHA-256 6d70a085df5909fd72a64490066c3453f345a87ff23adc2d36efe2208cdb41cd). It first entered the archive in unsigned commit f403afb9e6db2a2fb3825c7b4801c2af0ddd7228 on 24 April 2024; the embedded 2013 timestamp is not independently authenticated by custody. The ten-log census finds only three executed DH requests (118818811, 5, 3301); only the March 3301 record has an executed NEXT request, whose separate signature does not sign the surrounding log. The January exchange has no signed NEXT or authenticated client identity. Under the signed protocol the modulus/client public share are client-supplied and the server base/secret are participant-selected, so this record is not a creator-authenticated LP2 key or selector.


**Limit on the March DH3301/2800 match.** LP2 work source-selects the numeral 3301 and its p55/p56 terminal page-pair receiver; it does not independently authenticate the March participant log's client share 2800 or shared value 1067 as key material. The p57-to-p50 bridge to 2800 remains conditional on zero-based row-major and inner-to-outer reading; [#1565](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/issues/1565) leaves the order unresolved and [#1576](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/issues/1576) finds no independent pre-May-2014 exact-field witness. The exact 2800/1067 tuple is present only in the participant-preserved March log, which is not signed as a whole.

**Additional 2013 participant record used for the ICMP reconstruction:** [`irc-logs/#33012013.freenode.log`](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/irc-logs/%2333012013.freenode.log) at commit `ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3` (13,345,841 bytes; 190,170 lines; SHA-256 `3589f67c010e3290845900d1247ae1d65919859bb05e7e5efffb90b70dc46028`). It documents the `li498-122` / `106.187.103.122` association, the 15 January ICMP responder behavior, and the missing-PCAP discussion. It is a channel transcript, not a packet capture. See `im-results/2013-icmp-echo-packet-reconstruction.md`.

## cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada

Repository: https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada

A community historical archive of Cicada stages and artifacts. Particularly useful paths:

- [2014 stage 7](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/2014/007-fifth-onion/README.md): the documented human solve path uses audio/OpenPuff to obtain magic squares, then OutGuess to extract a Gödel theorem equation, an Escher eye, and a Bach Trio Sonata excerpt. These identify Gödel, Escher, Bach; the subsequent book cipher uses dialogue:speech:word:letter coordinates. The source text is named before book-code extraction.
- [2014 stage 10 hidden-service reply](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/2014/010-hidden-service-reply/README.md): preserves the reply and next onion-service address.
- [2014 stage 11 / Liber Primus](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/2014/011-seventh-onion/README.md): documents the 58 LP2 pages 0–57, the totient-shift solution for page 56, the plaintext page 57, and the unresolved “An End” hash continuation.

The archive is a community reconstruction, not a substitute for checking original image/audio bytes. The 2014 GEB chain is a strong precedent for clue-constrained book ciphers: do not transplant its book or coordinate convention to LP2 without a corresponding source-selection clue.


## Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis (pinned 7 November 2026)

Repository: https://github.com/Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis/tree/0b907164e95e3a44ee74c1d28efbf4688b770865

- Independent September 6–7, 2026 session; repository last pushed 7 November. It reproduces the nine established solved sections and reports no LP2 plaintext.
- Reports the 12,956-rune / 86-adjacent-repeat fingerprint, flat nonzero first-difference stream, no detected periodicity to its stated limits, and no shared keystream between sections. Its proposed chain model, c_i=c_(i-1)+s_i with nonzero 28-way steps and a rare zero event, is a **candidate explanation**, not an identified cipher or plaintext.
- Its source/key hunt includes OutGuess on all 75 images with no key and 96 candidate keys (4,521 nonempty outputs; unsolved-page outputs are 58,152-byte high-entropy noise), 692,438 archived candidates plus OutGuess payloads against the p56 target, and raw JPEG / growing-string running-key scans. These are useful prior-art negatives; overlap with other repositories and this project's later tests is not fully independent.
- Start with [REPORT.md](https://github.com/Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis/blob/0b907164e95e3a44ee74c1d28efbf4688b770865/docs/REPORT.md), [FINDINGS.md](https://github.com/Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis/blob/0b907164e95e3a44ee74c1d28efbf4688b770865/docs/FINDINGS.md), and [OutGuess / hash-source results](https://github.com/Leo-Y-Zhang/LiberPrimusAnalysis/blob/0b907164e95e3a44ee74c1d28efbf4688b770865/outguess/RESULTS.md). The repository declares an "Other" source-available license; inspect it before reusing code.

## micheloosterhof/aldegonde (independent LP2 transcription and word-clock hypothesis)

Repository: https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde

An independent LP2 transcription and experimental cryptanalysis repository. Its master transcription cross-checks the 15,933-rune manuscript total and 12,956-rune unsolved body. Its `data/page0-56.txt` retains punctuation/structural marks that are not all preserved by the normalized transcription here; use it as a secondary transcription, not as an authority. The repository's tokenizer yields a different word segmentation from this project's 2,896-word convention, so never silently mix word indices or word-clock results between them.

Relevant material:

- [Corpus conventions](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/data/README.rst) and [marked LP2 transcription](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/data/page0-56.txt).
- [Length-clocked walk hypothesis](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/hypotheses/length-clocked-walk.md): proposes a within-word order-five permutation, a word-dependent base permutation updated using word lengths, and an adjacent-repeat suppressor. This is a candidate forward model, not a recovered cipher or plaintext.
- [Per-word shift investigation](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/hypotheses/walk-with-per-word-shift.md) and [bounded sweep](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/experiments/walk_shift_sweep.py): explore source-keyed alphabets and word-clock updates; no authentic key or verified plaintext is reported.
- [Magic-square grid sweep](https://github.com/micheloosterhof/aldegonde/blob/main/experiments/magic_square_sweep.py): tests order-five permutations derived from the LP1 5×5 / 3301 square. Treat its outputs as model searches, not evidence that the square selects a unique permutation.
- The repository's within-word lag-five position analysis is a useful objection to a single global order-five map; it constrains candidate models but does not itself decrypt the text.

This is valuable independent prior art for punctuation, word-boundary, and order-five hypotheses. Do not repeat its broad grid/key sweeps without a new source-visible selector. Check the repository's license before reusing code or datasets.
 
## Cicada Notebook (104-session independent research notebook; updated 30 October 2026)

Guide: https://cicadanotebook.com/guide.html

The guide reports 104 focused sessions and no verified LP2 plaintext, decoding table, or author identity. These sessions are useful prior art, not proof of an LP2 solution. Particularly relevant:

- [Session 12 — 2012 Agrippa book-code reconstruction](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/12.html): reports a complete historical destination reproduction from a pre-puzzle text snapshot. The fixed convention is one-based line:character, beginning at the first verse line (excluding title/byline), treating HTML `<br>` as line breaks, stripping source indentation, and preserving blank verse lines, internal spaces, and punctuation. This is evidence for a real historical coordinate convention only; it does **not** select the 2016 GP-word-sum `29q+r` selector or Agrippa as an LP2 key.
- [Session 11 — published Agrippa algorithm test](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/11.html): applies the documented algorithm to the LP2 256-byte block and reports no readable ASCII output under the tested alignment. This does not exclude binary/compressed output, a different representation, or Agrippa used as a source text.
- [Session 104 — historical 2014 square submission](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/104.html): reports that all 40 original line totals verify, while each of the three squares has four distinct arrangements preserving dimensions, multiset, and magic totals. Actual server acceptance and MP3 extraction remain archival claims rather than newly reproduced operations; no matrix traversal is promoted to a cipher.
- [Session 55 — tree passage structure](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/55.html) and [Session 62 — derived boundary map](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/62.html): useful page-structure references, not a recovered key or traversal.
- [Session 65 — Berkeley remailer comparison](https://cicadanotebook.com/sessions/65.html): expands the comparison to 28 distinct verified message bodies and 94 solved-text clauses; reports no shared four-word phrase. The sample is not exhaustive.

Use the session-specific source captures and reproduction artifacts before importing a claim. The most useful distinction for current work is that historical one-based line:character indexing is documented, but a 2016 `29q+r` word-sum address still needs its own source selector.
## SECRA — Inside Liber Primus (15 October 2026)

Article: https://secra.tech/research/liber-primus-strongest-findings/

Supporting measurements: https://secra.tech/research/liber-primus-strongest-findings/evidence/index.html

- The page-57 mayfly dots strongly match a historical GIMP Dissolve / GLib random-field pattern: reported whole-image F1 **0.9601**, held-out F1 **0.9391**, with **166** cells still differing. The seed **314159265** is a GIMP software default, not evidence of a puzzle-selected π key. This is a rendering fingerprint, not a plaintext or cipher key.
- The archived 2014 *Interconnectedness* MP3 contains a repeated opening/ending noise waveform separated by **11,559,607 samples** (about **262.122608 s** at 44.1 kHz). Controlled cancellation did not reveal a supported additional message or key; the separate archived OpenPuff payload is a different channel.
- Three earlier magic squares have prescribed line sums 3301, 1033 and 1033. The community-observed center sequence 809, 331, 91 gives π-count differences 73 and 43 (GP letters L/P), but the article explicitly does **not** establish that center selection, prime counting and subtraction were uniquely instructed by Cicada.
- These findings overlap the current GIMP-confound assessment in `results/README.md`; do not reopen the retired p57 241/331 selector or audio residual search without the exact missing source artifact or a new independent selector. The article reports no LP2 decryption, key or destination.

## Additional modern research and tooling (reviewed 21 November 2026)

These sources were inspected for post-2018 claims of unknown-page plaintext or keys. None supplies a verified LP2 p0–55 decryption. Keep tools, candidate models, and actual plaintext recovery separate.

### Dukotah/cicada3301 — Round44 p15-grid and W2-B3 doublet-gap prior art (9–20 November 2026)

- Repository: https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301
- [Round44 P2 preregistration](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/main/liber-primus/analysis/round44/P2-p15-grid/PREREG.md) and [results](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/main/liber-primus/analysis/round44/P2-p15-grid/RESULTS.md) re-transcribe the original p15 4×4 grid and run **670,120** original-input decodes over all 55 unsolved pages, with three planted controls passing. The fixed family covers direct repeating/one-shot mod-29 keys, period-16 rank transpositions, and grid-seeded prime/totient ladders; it produces zero threshold crossers.
- Explicitly not covered there: F-interrupter/skip/rejection-loop compositions, spiral/diagonal/boustrophedon traversals, non-decimal digit readings, line-indexed selection, page-specific different keys, or combination with other presentation channels. Use this as a strong bounded negative, not as a proof that the p15 numerals have no possible role and not as an LP2 solution.
- This prior art is useful because it identifies exactly which p15-grid consumers were tested and which transition models remain outside the external sweep. No unknown plaintext or authentic key is claimed.

- [W2-B3 doublet-site preregistration](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-B3-doublet-sites/PREREG.md), [results](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-B3-doublet-sites/RESULTS.md), and [T7 queue](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-B3-doublet-sites/ORACLE-T7-QUEUE.md) report 86 adjacent-equal sites in 12,956 runes, gap ac1 +0.380, and a global site-matched p=0.0010; T7-void/T7-mechanism remain open. The external [SOLVERS-DOSSIER](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/SOLVERS-DOSSIER.md) argues the stream continues across word/clause/line/page boundaries. Local prior work already tests the claim against chapter, page, 13-dot, word/line, word-length, page-half, and exact printed-line conditioning: see [source-boundary gate](../../im-results/lp2-doublet-gap-source-boundary-conditional-gate.md), [printed-line occupancy audit](../../im-results/lp2-doublet-gap-original-source-conditioned.md), and [word-identity analysis](../../im-results/lp2-word-boundary-doublet-analysis.md). Treat T7 as an unresolved event-process observation, not an established stateful generator or recovered key.
  
### ZzNible/cicada3301-liber-primus-findings (11 September 2026)

- **Pinned [one-commit release](https://github.com/ZzNible/cicada3301-liber-primus-findings/tree/e0e77e99e8736082f7808e382f36225e0ef6f646)** (five Markdown files, no public experiment code or raw simulations). The author explicitly reports **no unknown LP2 plaintext, key, reset rule, or decryption mechanism**. Its 12,956-rune / 86-adjacent-equality and within-word lag-five **104/2,105** observations agree with already tracked local source fingerprints. The [FINDINGS](https://github.com/ZzNible/cicada3301-liber-primus-findings/blob/e0e77e99e8736082f7808e382f36225e0ef6f646/FINDINGS.md) claim a conditioned max-lag p≈0.008604 under a fixed doublet count, but the public release does **not** include the private null draws, code, or preregistration needed to reproduce that exact p-value. The local [frozen original-cipher predictor](../../im-results/lag5-lag6-heldout-conditional-prediction.md) already tests related dependencies with different controls; neither result identifies a cipher.
- The independent package-boundary discussion compares old LP1 source scans 00–16 with 58 Onion7 source scans 17–74. A claimed May 2014 byte-identical source lineage and 2014 Git history are useful provenance references, but the locally [authenticated May-2014 Onion7 HTML](../../results/README.md) and prior byte-matched [original-onion7 corpus](https://github.com/krisyotam/cicada3301/tree/76d3ee8c762f60025822c8c05edbf31351636469/liber-primus/original-onion7) already provide overlapping controls. The pre-Onion7 package boundary cannot by itself supply an LP2 reset or value-changing operation. Its seven-number historical basket is explicitly retrospective and has no cipher selector. This publication adds no ready-to-test authentic key.

### TheronEagle/liber-primus-research (30 September 2026)

The author's earlier 24–25 September blanket claims that all reasonable families had been ruled out are too broad for the reported sweeps.

It cannot reject page-local, evolving or nonlinear keys. The source's “missing scanned page 67” maps to **LP2 physical p50**, the known **256-cell base60 numeric page with zero runes**, so 55 rune-bearing unsolved pages / 12,956 runes is the expected GP-only scope; p50 remains an unsolved *non-rune* object. The independent [scorer audit](https://github.com/TheronEagle/liber-primus-research/blob/a6c5d13f7591030367daace993c887af20a5e0ab/experiments/2026-09-30/scorer_audit.json) corrects a 40.9%-based unambiguous spelling ceiling to 78.9% ambiguity-aware on solved pages, which improves its own negative controls but yields no LP2 inversion.
- **Crosswalk decision:** no authentic original-source operand, unknown-page plaintext, source-selected reversible receiver or independently new instruction is present in either inspected repository. Do not launch copied key sweeps or promote the finite negative tests to global impossibility; re-open only if a later commit introduces a specific new source-selected cipher mechanism or first-party archival object.

- **Pinned source:** [47f32a9e94061953ab25fdd5052996c27a86c002](https://github.com/jaxonkuipers/cicada3301/tree/47f32a9e94061953ab25fdd5052996c27a86c002), last committed 8 September 2026. No repository licence is declared; **link to implementations, do not copy the code**.

It reports a 136–678× speedup over its older beam and uses a score prior at approximately 40% true interrupters. [`tests/test_search.py`](https://github.com/jaxonkuipers/cicada3301/blob/47f32a9e94061953ab25fdd5052996c27a86c002/tests/test_search.py) includes genuine solved-text comparisons and planted/exhaustive tests, with exact recovery of chosen synthetic skips. This external implementation would matter *only if an independently original-source-selected key and clock* turn ambiguous F placement into the limiting inference problem. Then run its existing `python -m unittest tests.test_search` controls against source-native solved LP1, freeze the key and evaluate withheld original LP2 with a wrong-key comparator. Running it as a new dictionary/key sweep now has no causal path to plaintext.

Searchable prior-art discussions could prevent duplicated tests or expose a missing archival pointer; these are modern participant discussions, **not original Cicada-authenticated source**. No new LP2 plaintext/key is claimed. The route-owned [2014 public-release record](https://github.com/jaxonkuipers/cicada3301/blob/47f32a9e94061953ab25fdd5052996c27a86c002/corpus/records/R14.7/README.md) acknowledges the original decoder is unknown and its 2014 private recipient callback is missing.

#### Later master-branch elimination ledger (inspected 11 November 2026; document reports work through 29 July 2026)

The [master-branch ELIMINATION-LEDGER](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/ELIMINATION-LEDGER.md) adds materially relevant work beyond the pinned snapshot above. Treat its findings as external, not independently reproduced in this repository:

- **Filter-aware key-skip decoding:** [Campaign XVIII](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/master/liber-primus/analysis/campaign18_skip) validates a beam decoder that tracks the key/plaintext desynchronization caused by an approximately 83% doublet-suppression filter. A planted correct key recovers at −4.15 / 100% while rigid alignment scores −7.24 / 8.5%; false-positive ceiling is −6.82 and planted-key recall 7/8. Re-running referenced texts, a 122-text corpus, and 88 additional literary texts under the skip-aware model reportedly yields zero hits (best −5.754 across the extended sweeps). This is a major prior-art constraint: do not repeat rigid-alignment running-key sweeps or build a duplicate beam decoder without a materially different key source or forward model.
- **Themed-word/no-repeat combiner:** the external authors test 58 LP-thematic words, both signs, through a no-repeat combiner on 13 scorable unsolved pages; best long-page score −6.88, with a lossy 4.4% rejection rate. They close this particular family. This is more specific than the earlier keyless no-repeat statistic.
- **p49–51 table as per-section index and red-join reset:** [H1/H2 report](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/master/liber-primus/analysis/recon/lp2h_index) tests the 256-token base-60 table as an index/offset over 14 red-section-head pages, 11 decode models, and red-boundary continuity. The reported best score is −7.200; index concentration fails correction, base-60 geometry fails, and red joins show no reset (permutation p=1.0). This is an external negative not yet independently reproduced here; avoid duplicating the same 14-page index or red-join tests.
- **Transcription and corpus scope:** Campaign XIV reports the apparent ~75-page gap is already-solved material and pages 0–55 are the complete unsolved corpus; Campaign XV reports a label-free glyph-shape audit (ARI 0.75, homogeneity approaching 0.98), with only a fragile p24 local-172 glyph distinction. These are external claims; compare page numbering and exact corpus boundaries before importing counts.
- **External frontier stated by that ledger:** its authors retain an untried already-public keytext and recovery of the AN END deep-web page; they report internal ciphertext-only attacks exhausted. Their [OSINT sweep](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/analysis/OSINT-SWEEP-2026-07-27.md) is relevant prior art for the Tor2web archive question.
- **Tor2web Wayback correction:** the same OSINT-SWEEP document explicitly records: “Wayback/tor2web (.onion.to/.city) = DEAD END: only saved the gateway ‘temporarily not available’ page.” Its preceding list includes ky2khlqdf7qdznac among the archived onion sites. This is an external reported negative, not independently reproduced in our repository. Agent35's later target-specific check of the preserved ky2khlqdf7qdznac.onion.to CDX snapshot found only the root and robots.txt, with no page-59 path. Therefore the generic .onion.to/.city proxy-CDX class is not unexamined; any remaining archival task must name a narrower proxy, URL, or capture not covered by those checks. The [p56 source/hash gate](../../im-results/lp2-p56-hash-2016-signed-tree-source-gate.md) records the earlier runtime's direct CDX-access limitation, not evidence that the external class had never been checked.

The older [OPEN-AVENUES](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/master/liber-primus/analysis/OPEN-AVENUES.md) file is dated 17 June 2026 and still lists independent vision re-transcription as top priority; the later Campaign XV label-free audit is the relevant follow-up, so do not repeat that June recommendation as if it were still untouched. The master-branch ledger is a large external measurement program, not proof that LP2 is literally a one-time pad or that plaintext cannot exist.

#### Round44 master snapshot and local crosswalk (inspected 14 November 2026)

- **Pinned current master:** [9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29), committed 12 November. [Round44 synthesis](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round44/SYNTHESIS.md) reports 22 executed cells and no solve.
- **B3/T7 external anomaly:** [results](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-B3-doublet-sites/RESULTS.md) measure 86 adjacent-equal sites and gap lag-1 Pearson +0.380, with matched-null p=0.0010 (10,000 draws) and independent X1 p=0.00025. The same cell's doubled-value, gap, and position channel reads are negative at measured power; T7 is an ordering statistic, not a recovered message. [C5](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-C5-stationarity/RESULTS.md) finds no detectable per-page heterogeneity at its registered power, while explicitly leaving sub-page ordering open.
- **Local reconciliation (do not repeat or misread T7):** our [block-marginal control](../../im-results/lp2-doublet-block-marginal-control.md) finds the 13-bin 1,000-rune block dispersion ordinary (flat-site p=0.197516; page×word-length×role p=0.503975). The +0.380 gap correlation is largely inherited from which 85 printed words carry the events (word-identity conditional p=0.259137; see [source-boundary gate](../../im-results/lp2-doublet-gap-source-boundary-conditional-gate.md)); exact printed-line occupancy gives a saturated descriptive p=0.231944 (see [line-scale report](../../im-results/lp2-doublet-gap-original-source-conditioned.md)). These source-conditioned results do not support a nonstationary key schedule, line cipher, or predictive state. No plaintext/key was found.
- **Direction-channel prior art:** the master [ELIMINATION-LEDGER](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/ELIMINATION-LEDGER.md) records R22-B's 72 generic per-page turtle/direction renders as a control-validated null; R9-DIRECTION's 2,670 positional reads lacked a positive control and R40-C1 later demoted the page/region variants below the near-miss rule; R37-C1's composed 2016 map→road→direction settings remained below score bars. Do not repeat generic turtle, positional, or signed-clause direction searches.
- **p49–51 canonical bytes:** the local 256 integers in resources/liber-primus/base60-grid.json match the external [Campaign VII canon_256.hex](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/pp49_51/canon_256.hex) byte-for-byte (256/256). This corroborates the token-derived stream, not an independent re-reading of original glyphs; the external ledger notes six token/decimal witness disputes. None of the local exploratory GEM-basin positions intersects those six disputed positions.
- The local p50 proposal to split each base-60 token as B=29q+r and interpret q+1 through the repeated 4-corner + 5-cross page ornament is a **distinct exploratory operation**, not a result reported in the cited external direction tests. Keep it provisional; it must produce a locked plaintext prediction rather than another generic direction sweep.

## 2014 primary-source archive crosswalk and acquisition priorities (reviewed 19 November 2026)

This crosswalk separates authenticated Cicada messages from community reconstructions, identifies exact source objects missing from `resources/`, and avoids counting forks or mirrored copies as independent evidence.

### Verified 2014 source-selection controls

- **Stage 1 — Self-Reliance book code.** The signed message [`2014/001-twitter/zN4h51m.jpg.asc`](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/001-twitter/zN4h51m.jpg.asc) is 1,150 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 `1f9a61b97d5de9c4ca57402c064365a503d956a9`. Its OpenPGP signature verifies under the established Cicada key fingerprint `6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F` (signature timestamp 2014-01-06 04:59:26 UTC). The poem points to Emerson's *Self-Reliance*; the same stage contains the [archived source text](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/001-twitter/self-reliance.txt) and a [community `book-code.py` implementation](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/001-twitter/book-code.py). Reimplementing the documented one-indexed paragraph:sentence:word:letter extraction, including the paragraph-offset correction for the inserted excerpt from paragraph 45 onward, reproduces `auqgnxjtvdbll3pv.onion`. This is a verified historical solve path, not an LP2 key or permission to transplant its coordinate convention without an LP2 source-selection clue.
- **Stage 2 — explicit RSA-OAEP.** The signed [`2014/002-first-onion/1033.jpg.asc`](https://github.com/neuroretransmit/cicada/blob/ade9a02889ef8acbc8cde8edbfd0a785c369f4c3/2014/002-first-onion/1033.jpg.asc) is 1,498 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 `cd529671eac6458a790f047d23895af264b11751` (the same blob appears as `messages/2014/welcome.asc` in iBotPeaches). Its signature verifies under the same key (2014-01-06 07:35:27 UTC). The message supplies `e = 65537`, a modulus, and explicitly labels the compressed ciphertext `Crypt::RSA::ES::OAEP`. This is evidence of clue-selected, recognizable operations in the earlier round, not an LP2 decryption.
- The two verified Stage 1/2 messages are exact duplicate blobs in the iBotPeaches archive; that mirror is not a second independent signature or discovery. **Stage 3/4 XOR chain:** the [00.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/003-second-onion/00.jpg.asc), [01.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/003-second-onion/01.jpg.asc), and [02.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/003-second-onion/02.jpg.asc) page messages are the inputs named by the [Stage 4 README](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/004-first-three-pages/README.md); it describes XORing them to obtain the `IDGTK...` ciphertext. iBotPeaches carries [idgtk-umloo.asc](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/cicada_3301/blob/09a6fa4848e5943dbb48c738584f2ec8442ec2a4/messages/2014/idgtk-umloo.asc) (989 bytes; SHA-1 `3c42f017cadb94b90f08e04d3e85908384e39a71`), whose signature remains unverified in this audit. Its [hello-you-have-done-well.asc](https://github.com/iBotPeaches/cicada_3301/blob/09a6fa4848e5943dbb48c738584f2ec8442ec2a4/messages/2014/hello-you-have-done-well.asc) (1,351 bytes; Git blob SHA-1 `14470df9fd76f4d1599ab12e63b77d1a143d46af`) is exactly the pinned Sixth Onion `v2-form.html.asc` signed response plus one trailing LF. The pinned 1,350-byte object and this mirror both verify under Cicada fingerprint `6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F` at 2014-01-25 08:26:57 UTC; they are one signed body, not two independent instructions. The pinned original is preserved as `resources/historical/cicada2014-sixth-onion-v2-form.html.asc`.
- **Stage 6/9 secondary records.** [Stage 6 `08.jpg.asc`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/006-fourth-onion/08.jpg.asc) is a 140-byte unsigned grouped-text prompt (“For those who have fallen behind”); do not treat it as PGP-authenticated. The [Stage 9 submission pages](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/tree/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/009-squares-submission-pages) include `107.jpg`, `167.jpg`, and `229.jpg`; the community README reports `FIRFUMFERENFE` as the Vigenère key for the first two and an unencrypted third page. They are not in `resources/` and remain historical context, not an LP2 key.
- **Sixth Onion signed square-submission request (2014/008-sixth-onion).** The pinned [11.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/008-sixth-onion/11.jpg.asc), [12.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/008-sixth-onion/12.jpg.asc), and [13.jpg.asc](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/008-sixth-onion/13.jpg.asc) messages are now preserved in `resources/historical/`. Each is 1,234 bytes; their Git blob SHA-1s are `2f825249d5d37555053abf3b07d2fe8fb1def56b`, `7d883e03ece7823fbfcfe906461084c55ea1525b`, and `4cff459f0d0d6abb4c1d8879591fd085e420877a`; all three independently report GOODSIG/VALIDSIG under Cicada fingerprint `6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F`, signed 2014-01-19 07:39:42/50/57 UTC. Their signed bodies ask solvers to create a Tor hidden service accepting CGI uploads, submit three already-obtained magic squares plus the service URL, and work alone. They specify no square-generation rule, ordering, traversal, arithmetic, key, or LP2 receiver. The embedded framed 3×3 arrays are not magic squares under row/column/diagonal sums; the community README calls them OutGuess frames, which is an unsigned reconstruction. The same pinned folder's signed [v2-form response](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/b13600373d3400d75ec4208198019f3d92a304dd/2014/008-sixth-onion/ut3qtzbrvs7dtvzp.onion.v2-form.html.asc) is 1,350 bytes (Git blob `ff4d21ad4e56836070f431a6a297ab14a10a099b`; SHA-256 `8de5d05fccdaa3c087ce70eea44fba27f7cac9db290a46a0672ab717a0ebbfc0`) and verifies at 2014-01-25 08:26:57 UTC. It specifies the participant-side `/cgi-bin/upload` path, file input `file`, and participant public key `/key.asc`; this is distinct from Cicada's Stage 10 `/cgi-bin/squares` endpoint. The existing 99-number source is three actual squares (5×5/3301, 7×7/1033, 5×5/1033) and matches the Stage 10 form fields, but the signed request does not explain their derivation. See [source audit](../../im-results/cicada2014-sixth-onion-square-request-source-audit.md) and [SFT](../../sims/cicada2014_sixth_onion_square_request_sft.py). The adjacent `cgi/key.asc` is a participant-submitted key, not the Cicada signing key.
- The 2014 Stage 10 reply is already represented by `resources/historical/cicada2014-stage11-message.asc`; do not reacquire it merely because another archive uses a different filename or whitespace.

### Stage 7 Interconnectedness carrier — highest-priority missing source

Two separate archives, [`cijhho123`](https://github.com/cijhho123/cicada3301/tree/d360ad97d39c4719e42dc88b0cbbb81ed54aa02c/assets/2014/stage07) and [`scream314`](https://github.com/scream314/cicada3301/tree/10733feb487bb8beb9966d534727ee5897aa54fc/assets/2014/stage07), contain byte-identical objects:

- Original signed-hex page: [cijhho `index.html`](https://github.com/cijhho123/cicada3301/blob/d360ad97d39c4719e42dc88b0cbbb81ed54aa02c/assets/2014/stage07/q4utgdi2n4m4uim5.onion/index.html), 13,526,359 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 `afb1ae7b8ffe2def6d1cd7a2f7ce961e550331b9`.
- Derived [cijhho `index.mp3`](https://github.com/cijhho123/cicada3301/blob/d360ad97d39c4719e42dc88b0cbbb81ed54aa02c/assets/2014/stage07/index.mp3) / “3301 - Interconnectedness.mp3”: 6,651,873 bytes, Git blob SHA-1 `09fe068192b76a3697c47ec1d604b527703db798`.
- Derived `magicsquares.txt`: 721 bytes in cijhho (SHA-1 `bc26dcc8bf6c6da12fa16006374831225fe225da`) and 745 bytes in scream314 (SHA-1 `0cff0a94f16a8603443619b6338def411c9f7bd5`). The byte representations differ, but their 99-number streams are identical.

The matching blob hashes across these repositories are a byte-identity cross-check, not proof of two independent first-party captures; both are community archives. The cijhho Stage 7 README documents GPG verification followed by hexadecimal decoding (`gpg < index.html | xxd -r -p > index.mp3`). The cicada-solvers Stage 7 README documents the subsequent OpenPuff v4.00 extraction using password `33011033`, B/C disabled, and 50% bit selection, yielding the three magic squares before the GEB/OutGuess route. The original signed-hex page and derived MP3 are absent from this repository's `resources/`. The 745-byte scream314 `magicsquares.txt` payload is already preserved as [`resources/cicada2014-openpuff-magic-squares.txt`](../cicada2014-openpuff-magic-squares.txt) (blob SHA-1 `0cff0a94f16a8603443619b6338def411c9f7bd5`); the 721-byte cijhho variant has the same 99-number stream. Only the carrier page/MP3 are missing locally, not the derived square data. The archive recipe has not yet been independently rerun here; the exact hashes make this a bounded, reproducible acquisition task. It is a prior-stage receiver/key-selection chain, not new LP2 plaintext. The Stage07 signed-hex page's OpenPGP signature packet creation-time subpacket decodes to 2014-01-18 01:03:57 UTC; the separate 2014-01-upload-instructions message is signed 2014-01-25 08:26:57 UTC, and the four magic-square-upload OutGuess variants are signed 2014-01-19. The first grid is exactly the 5×5/3301 matrix printed on LP1 p16 image16.jpg; LP2 p22 image39.jpg does not print the matrix. The preserved file is plain row-major data, with no caption or special center/edge convention. The 2014 upload instructions ask for three magic squares and a Tor service; they do not specify a center extraction, radix, or LP2 table consumer.

### LP2 byte and transcription controls; duplicates to retire

- The 58 `2014onion7/0.jpg`–`57.jpg` originals in cijhho match `resources/liber-primus/17.jpg`–`74.jpg` byte-for-byte (58/58). Its `2014/Liber Primus/runes in text format.txt` is also the exact same Git blob as `resources/transcriptions/lp2_krisyotam_2017.txt` (43,739 bytes; SHA-1 `43bfeb6bf8dabaf25b0446cc519f8d91d205d8a7`). This archive adds no new LP2 image bytes or rune sequence.
- The 58 Stage 11 images in the cicada-solvers reconstruction are differently encoded variants; do not substitute them for the local originals.
- iBotPeaches' 2016 `hello-the-path-lies-empty.asc` and 2017 `beware-false-paths.asc` are formatting variants of the already-preserved and authenticated `cicada2016-4gq25-outguess.asc` and `cicada2017-yEiTHhvF.asc`. No new message content or key material was found there. The existing 2012–2013 20-message signature audit also remains the controlling record; do not repeat it.
- scream314 carries the full 75-page image set; the repository's `resources/liber-primus/` currently tracks the 58 LP2 pages (physical images 17–74), not the first 17 LP1 pages. Those earlier pages are historical context, not new LP2 ciphertext.

### Acquisition order

1. **Stage 7 signed page + MP3.** Highest value: obtain the exact carrier objects above, verify the page signature with the established key, reproduce GPG→hex→MP3, rerun OpenPuff, and compare the extracted 99-number stream with the already-preserved `resources/cicada2014-openpuff-magic-squares.txt`. This restores the original carrier for the known magic-square receiver chain.
2. **Stage 3 signed page messages and Sixth Onion square-submission request.** The 11/12/13 objects and signed follow-up are now preserved and verified; they authenticate a three-square upload challenge, not a square-construction method or LP2 decoder. The three Stage 3 XOR input messages and `idgtk-umloo.asc` remain separate archival/signature questions. No direct LP2 key has been established.
3. **Stage 1/2 signed messages and Self-Reliance text.** Keep their hashes and reproducible route as a historical solve-path control. They are already publicly available and their signatures were verified; they do not justify unconstrained book-cipher searches in LP2.
4. **Stage 9 submission pages and Stage 6 unsigned grouped text.** Secondary context only; the latter lacks a Cicada signature and must not be promoted to authenticated evidence.
5. **Do not spend further effort reacquiring** the 58 LP2 originals, the rune transcript, or the 2016/2017 messages; their exact content is already present locally.

### F5 reference toolchain (grayscale-control caveat)

- [`0verkilll/f5`](https://github.com/0verkilll/f5) v1.0.0 provides coefficient-level F5 `embed`/`extract` and an `embed-jar` compatibility path. The latter is **RGB-only**: its `WriteBMP24` path feeds a Java reference encoder whose `JpegInfo.NumberOfComponents` is hard-coded to 3. Do not use `embed-jar` as a one-component grayscale positive control.
- [`0verkilll/jpeg`](https://github.com/0verkilll/jpeg) v1.0.1 has explicit one-component grayscale specs and a grayscale coefficient-encoding path. Its full coefficient-preservation regression covers 4:2:0/4:2:2/4:4:4 but omits grayscale; synthetic grayscale coefficient-encoding tests exist.
- Detailed source-level capability assessment and control requirements: [F5 reference implementation capabilities](f5-reference-implementation-capabilities.md). This is tooling prior art, not an LP2 payload finding.

### Historical onion-hash search tooling

- [martinlindhe/gohash](https://github.com/martinlindhe/gohash): a historical SHA-512 preimage-search tool whose README gives a base32 `.onion` brute-force example. Enumerating all 16-character base32 labels is (32^{16}=2^{80}), not a practical attack. Its bundled [eight-address candidate list](https://github.com/martinlindhe/gohash/blob/master/data/onion-sites.txt) was checked against the AN-END digest using SHA-512, SHA3-512 and BLAKE2b-512 over bare-address and URL forms; no match. This is a historical attempt, not evidence that the full address space was searched.

### Parcae and Rune Decrypter Prime

- [ToldByNun/Parcae](https://github.com/ToldByNun/Parcae): C++20 cryptanalysis toolkit with known-page regression fixtures; the README tutorial demonstrates Atbash on the already-solved “A Warning” page, not an unknown-page decryption.
- [mortlach/RuneDecrypterPrime](https://github.com/mortlach/RuneDecrypterPrime): reusable cipher/key/search framework; no verified unknown-page plaintext or authentic LP2 key surfaced in the inspected material.
- [mortlach/Liber-Primus-Crib-Assist](https://github.com/mortlach/Liber-Primus-Crib-Assist): crib-search tooling, not a recovered solution.

For the detailed claim-by-claim audit, including the unsupported 2026 “dynamic stream / geographic cipher” Reddit claim and the README-only “full translation” repository, see [modern-public-claim-audit-2026-11-11.md](../../im-results/modern-public-claim-audit-2026-11-11.md).

The four cited byte strings are each 512 hex characters; string 4 equals all **256** decoded pp49–51 original numeric-grid bytes under the existing base60 transcription.

### `cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools` — finite cuneiform-table stream hypothesis

- Repository: https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools
- Relevant files: [`secrets.py`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools/blob/main/secrets.py), [`experiments.py`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools/blob/main/experiments.py), [`transformers.py`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools/blob/main/transformers.py), [section definitions 011–015](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools/tree/main/liber_primus), and [`english_wordlist.txt`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/JBO-cicada_tools/blob/main/english_wordlist.txt).
- `secrets.py` defines a 256-token `CUNEIFORM_STREAM`; it matches the local `resources/liber-primus/lp2-grid-256.json` token sequence exactly. `experiments.py` tests it as a finite additive/subtractive GP29 keystream: base59/base60, all six digit/uppercase/lowercase chunk orders, forward/reverse, with `KeystreamTransformer` changing only the first 256 runes of each section. The external grouping marks sections 011–015 (pages23–55) as unsolved.
- Local evaluation: 48 variants × 5 sections = 240 cases, using the original local rune corpus and the external 69,904-line English wordlist. None reaches three consecutive dictionary words and normalized IoC 1.4; maximum prefix is one word and maximum IoC is 1.051969. See [the consolidated table256 report](../../im-results/lp2-cuneiform-1033-3301-table256-diagonal-original.md) and [the reproducible SFT](../../sims/lp2_cuneiform_table256_rowmajor_keystream_sft.cjs).
- The stream is a community interpretation of an existing table, not independent key material or a first-party cipher instruction. GitHub reports no declared license for this repository; do not vendor its code or wordlist.
